ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, point $E$ is on $AC$, the circle $O$ passing through points $A$, $B$, and $E$ intersects $BC$ at point $D$, and point $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BE$, with $AB$ being the diameter of the circle; if $AB=8$ and $\angle C=60^\circ$, what is the area of the shaded region?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Let $OF \perp BE$,\\
$\therefore \angle OFB=90^\circ$, $BE=2BF$,\\
$\because AB=AC$, $\angle C=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle BAC=60^\circ$,\\
$\because \overset{\frown}{BE}=\overset{\frown}{BE}$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOE=2\angle BAC=120^\circ$, $\angle AOE=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
$\because AB=8$,\\
$\therefore$ the radius of the circle is 4,\\
$\because OB=OE$, $\angle BOE=120^\circ$, $OF\perp BE$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOF= \frac{1}{2}\angle BOE=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle OBF=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OF= \frac{1}{2}OB=2$,\\
$\therefore BF=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore BE=4\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\text{shaded part}}= S_{\text{sector} AOE}+S_{\triangle BOE}=\frac{60^\circ \pi \times 4^2}{360}+\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 4\sqrt{3}=\boxed{\frac{8}{3}\pi +4\sqrt{3}}$

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, point $E$ is on $AC$, the circle $O$ passing through points $A$, $B$, and $E$ intersects $BC$ at point $D$, and point $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BE$, with $AB$ being the diameter of the circle; if $AB=8$ and $\angle C=60^\circ$, what is the area of the shaded region?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:}

Let $OF \perp BE$,\\
$\therefore \angle OFB=90^\circ$, $BE=2BF$,\\
$\because AB=AC$, $\angle C=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle BAC=60^\circ$,\\
$\because \overset{\frown}{BE}=\overset{\frown}{BE}$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOE=2\angle BAC=120^\circ$, $\angle AOE=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
$\because AB=8$,\\
$\therefore$ the radius of the circle is 4,\\
$\because OB=OE$, $\angle BOE=120^\circ$, $OF\perp BE$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOF= \frac{1}{2}\angle BOE=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle OBF=90^\circ-60^\circ=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore OF= \frac{1}{2}OB=2$,\\
$\therefore BF=\sqrt{4^2-2^2}=2\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore BE=4\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore S_{\text{shaded part}}= S_{\text{sector} AOE}+S_{\triangle BOE}=\frac{60^\circ \pi \times 4^2}{360}+\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 4\sqrt{3}=\boxed{\frac{8}{3}\pi +4\sqrt{3}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure there is a circle, the center is marked as O, A is above the circle, B is at the lower left of the circle, and segment AB passes through O, appearing as the diameter of the circle. Point E is located on the lower right side and on AC, and the circle passes through A, B, and E; point D is on BC. The shaded region can correspondingly be decomposed into two parts: sector AOE and triangle BOE.

Reasoning: Because AB=AC and ∠C=60°, the base angles of isosceles triangle ABC are ∠B=∠C=60°, hence ∠A=60°, that is, △ABC is an equilateral triangle. Therefore, when E is on AC, ∠BAE=∠BAC=60°. In circle O, ∠BAE is the inscribed angle subtending arc BE, so the corresponding central angle ∠BOE=2∠BAE=120°. Also because AB is a diameter, ∠AOB=180°, hence ∠AOE=180°-120°=60°. Given AB=8, the radius r=4. Shaded area = area of sector AOE + area of △BOE. The area of sector AOE is (60/360)π·4^2=8π/3. The area of △BOE is (1/2)·4·4·sin120°=4√3. So the shaded area is 8π/3+4√3.
